subject: Context split & $/1M tokens — follow-up + profile clarifications
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@clearshelf.io>, engineers@clearshelf.io
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 18:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: context split + rough $/1M estimate (recap)

Marta / Clearshelf engineering — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap while items are fresh and a couple of clarifying questions so we can lock down a pricing sketch for the pilot: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Two primary inference flows: agent-style search assistant (avg session: 3 prompts + 2 completions) and nightly batch summarization of product reviews.
- Typical user prompt lengths: 350–900 prompt tokens, completions range 150–1,200 depending on summary verbosity.
- You indicated ~150k monthly active users for the search assistant, with ~2 sessions/user/day (very rough). Batch job processes ~10M documents / month; sample size today ~50M tokens/month.
- Long-context requirement: a subset of use (customer transcripts) will need extended context—mostly 8k today, potential 32k in Q4 if transcripts stitched.

Open clarifications we need to finalize pricing ballpark:
1) Can you confirm average prompt tokens and completion tokens per flow (agent vs batch)? I attached token_profile.csv with sample buckets — please confirm or replace.
2) For the long-context use: how often will the agent request >8k context vs 8k vs 32k? Rough percentage is fine.
3) Budget envelope: do you have a target $/1M tokens (or target monthly spend) for an initial 3-month pilot? You mentioned a target <$1k per 1M in the call but also a target spend of $20–40k/month — want to align the math.

Next steps I propose:
- You review & return token_profile.csv with actual averages (or a sample export).
- We provide two pricing sketches (hosted pay-as-you-go and a pilot with reserved Dedicated capacity for predictable $/M).
- If we align on volume and context split, we’ll include quantization/throughput recommendations that materially change the unit economics.

Attachments: token_profile.csv (sample tokens by flow)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20m call to walk the file.

Best,
Jasmine
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 19:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: context split + rough $/1M estimate (recap)

Jasmine / Marta — adding a couple of internal notes on the economics side so we can prepare a realistic price band.

Quick asks to help our costing model: 
- Token mix: send the sample export (or confirm the CSV) split by flow (agent_search, nightly_batch, transcript_long). If you can include percent of requests that trigger KV-cache hits and average seq length to first token (cold vs warm cache) that would change the per-token latency/cost profile.
- Target SLOs: what latency is acceptable for agent responses? 200ms p50 vs 500ms p95 maps to different cluster sizes.
- For pilot sizing: are you open to a 3–6 month committed Dedicated pool (saves ~20–30% unit) vs hosted? We'll prepare both.

I'll attach a quick cost-model.xlsx skeleton that maps model family, context window (8k/32k/128k), avg prompt/comp tokens, and estimated $/1M tokens for hosted vs dedicated.

—Karthik
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference

Attachment stub: cost-model.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB)
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@clearshelf.io>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: engineers@clearshelf.io
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: context split + rough $/1M estimate (recap)

Thanks Jasmine — appreciate the summary. Quick clarifications from our side (answered inline):

- Agent search assistant:
  * Avg prompt tokens: 420
  * Avg completion tokens: 320 (usually concise answers)
  * Sessions: closer to 1.4 sessions/user/day (we overestimated in the call)
  * KV cache: ~65% cache hit for follow-ups (same session).
- Nightly batch summarization:
  * Avg prompt tokens (per doc batch): 1,100
  * Avg completion tokens: 850
  * These run outside latency constraints and can tolerate batching.
- Long context (transcripts):
  * Today: ~7% of requests need >8k context (we pad to 8k for many).
  * If we stitch transcripts in Q4, that could grow to ~22% needing 32k.

Budget notes: our procurement/finance pair have indicated an initial pilot budget of $18k–$30k/month; leadership wants to see projected $/1M tokens under both hosted and reserved scenarios before committing. The $1k per 1M figure we mentioned was aspirational — we expect realistic numbers may be higher for the long-context tranche.

I attached a small export (samples) — hope that helps. Happy for a 20m math call with Karthik/Vivek.

Best,
Marta
Head of Product | Clearshelf
marta@clearshelf.io

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: context split + rough $/1M estimate (recap)

Great — thanks Marta, that data is very helpful. Next steps and what we’ll send by end of week: 

1) Two pricing sketches:
   - Hosted (pay-as-you-go) with tiered $/1M for short/long contexts and a separate premium for 32k requests.
   - 3-month Dedicated pilot quote with committed capacity and a discount schedule — we’ll show breakeven points and what volumes make Dedicated clearly cheaper.
2) Concrete unit economics table: avg prompt tokens, avg comp tokens, activity factor, expected tokens/month, and headline $/1M for each tranche (agent, batch, long-context 8k, long-context 32k).
3) Ops note: if you can accept a flexible fallback policy (route to smaller context variant with summary when 32k is expensive), we can show ~25–40% cost improvement for that tranche.

Proposed quick call: Thu 1 Jul 2027 10:00am PT — 20m to walk the pricing deck. Let me know if that works.

I’ll attach the draft SLA and a filled blank of our cost-model so you can tweak assumptions.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning.

Jasmine
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
